title: The topsy-turvy galaxy NGC 1313
caption: Central region of the starburst galaxy NGC 1313, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 1313 · constellation Reticulum · about 20 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Green clouds and many knots of star formation crowd this view of the central parts of NGC 1313, a starburst galaxy. Its busy state is obvious at a glance, with star-forming regions everywhere.

A starburst galaxy is one making new stars at an unusually high rate. In NGC 1313, successive waves of star birth have blown and sculpted cocoons of gas called supershell nebulae, and the galaxy's centre holds a great many of them. The green patches mark gas glowing in the light of ionised oxygen, and they may hold clusters of very hot stars whose radiation makes the gas shine.

The picture was built from observations made using FORS1, an instrument mounted on one of the 8.2-metre Unit Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope at Cerro Paranal. Combining broad colour filters with narrow ones tuned to single glowing gases lets astronomers map where the energetic young stars are reshaping their surroundings.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (6.70 x 6.05 arcminutes) and distance (20 million light years), the frame spans roughly 39,000 × 35,000 light-years. Its light set out about 20 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This colour composite was made with the FORS1 instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope, combining broad-band visible and near-infrared filters with narrow-band filters for hydrogen and oxygen. The caption notes that green marks ionised oxygen, but the other colours' mapping is not published.
understand.eye: Narrow-band filters isolate light from single elements, and the long exposures gather far more light than the eye, so the glowing gas stands out much more than it would to an observer.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: The data were obtained on the night of 16 December 2003, through broad-band R, B and z filters and narrow-band filters including hydrogen-alpha and oxygen lines.
alt: The crowded centre of a galaxy with many bright star-forming knots and green glowing clouds of gas.
